raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A HiCache storage backend can keep a second form of the FULL pages in a side pool, stored as whole key groups at block boundaries (for example a compact encoding of a block of pages). Serving the head of a prefetch span from such groups and the tail as raw KV needs three small pieces of shared plumbing that the hybrid cache controller and the unified radix cache do not have today:

- a way for a side pool to report which pages its leading complete groups cover without gating the KV hit itself;
- a way for the hit-time plan to record how many KV pages it skips in front of the KV transfer (the device-head trim, then the span head the groups serve), so the raw transfer and its acknowledgement are placed after them;
- a way to queue an H2D copy into device rows the caller already owns, with KV-derived side pools bound to the caller's logical anchor rows rather than to the destination rows.

Separately, an allocation-driven FULL eviction currently frees exactly the allocator's reported shortfall. An allocator can hide freed headroom behind a clamp (a reserve it refills before raw allocation sees a page again) or page rounding, so freeing exactly the shortfall can leave the availability target unmet and the allocation still fails after the walk.

## Modifications

- `PoolHitPolicy.BLOCK_GROUPS`, with `block_pages` / `group_pages` on `PoolTransfer` describing the group geometry (FULL pages per block, keys per group). The pool's verdict is the pages its leading complete groups cover; it never gates the KV hit.
- `PrefetchOperation.prefetch_kv_page_offset` and `group_skip_pages`: the KV pages the hit-time plan skips ahead of the KV transfer. `trim_prefetch_full_head` advances the first by the pages it trims.
- `HybridCacheController.load` takes keyword-only `device_indices` (caller-owned destination rows, never allocated or freed by the load) and `anchor_indices` (what KV-derived side pools bind against; default is the KV destination rows).
- `UnifiedRadixCache` FULL eviction driven by an allocation target walks to the target: the walk quota becomes the whole evictable FULL set, and the per-victim target check still stops it at the first sufficient victim. Explicit `evict()` calls and non-FULL components keep the requested count.

Tests:

- `test_unified_radix_allocation_eviction.py`: the shared fixture now gives `tree_core.full_evictable_size()` a value (a bare mock made the new `max()` raise), plus a regression case where the first victim's frees stay hidden and the walk must continue to the target.
- `test_unified_hicache_transfer_lifecycle.py`: a load into caller-owned rows allocates nothing, keeps those rows when a side pool fails and the load rolls back, and binds a KV-derived side pool to the anchor rows.
- `test_hybrid_pool_assembler.py`: the trim subtests also check the page offset the trim leaves behind.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model forward code or kernels.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the only behavior change on existing paths is the FULL eviction walk under an allocation target, which stops at the same victim as before whenever freed pages become allocatable one-for-one.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -93,10 +93,15 @@ class PoolHitPolicy(str, Enum):
 
     ALL_PAGES      : every page in [0, kv_hit) must exist (e.g. DSA).
     TRAILING_PAGES : only the last N pages must exist (e.g. Mamba/SWA states).
+    BLOCK_GROUPS   : whole key groups at block boundaries from the span start
+                     (a second form of the FULL pages, e.g. compressed blocks).
+                     The pool reports the pages its leading complete groups
+                     cover as its own verdict; it never gates the KV hit.
     """
 
     ALL_PAGES = "all_pages"
     TRAILING_PAGES = "trailing_pages"
+    BLOCK_GROUPS = "block_groups"
 
 
 @dataclass
@@ -115,6 +120,9 @@ class PoolTransfer:
     hit_policy: PoolHitPolicy = PoolHitPolicy.ALL_PAGES
     nodes_to_load: Optional[List[Any]] = None
     indices_from_pool: Optional[PoolName] = None
+    # BLOCK_GROUPS geometry: FULL pages per block and keys (pages) per group.
+    block_pages: int = 0
+    group_pages: int = 0
 
 
 @dataclass(frozen=True)

@@ -156,6 +156,10 @@ def __init__(
         self._lock = threading.Lock()
         self._terminated_flag = False
         self.storage_hit_count = 0
+        # KV pages the hit-time plan skips in front of the KV transfer: the
+        # device trim, then the span head a component's block groups serve.
+        self.prefetch_kv_page_offset = 0
+        self.group_skip_pages = 0
         self.start_time = time.monotonic()
         # Take the whole span as present instead of querying for it; the read
         # itself is fail-soft, so a wrong guess shortens the fetch.
@@ -963,15 +967,25 @@ def load(
         priority: Optional[int] = None,
         node_id: int = -1,
         extra_pools: Optional[list[PoolTransfer]] = None,
+        *,
+        device_indices: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+        anchor_indices: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
     ) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+        """Queue an H2D of ``host_indices`` into freshly allocated FULL rows,
+        or into caller-owned ``device_indices`` (kept on failure); side pools
+        bind their device slots against ``anchor_indices`` (default: the KV
+        destination rows)."""
         need_load_kv = host_indices.numel() > 0
+        caller_owned = device_indices is not None
 
         full_allocator = getattr(
             self.mem_pool_device_allocator,
             "full_attn_allocator",
             self.mem_pool_device_allocator,
         )
-        if not need_load_kv:
+        if caller_owned:
+            assert len(device_indices) == len(host_indices)
+        elif not need_load_kv:
             device_indices = torch.empty((0,), dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device)
         else:
             device_indices = full_allocator.alloc(len(host_indices))
@@ -980,11 +994,13 @@ def load(
 
         pool_transfers = self._resolve_device_transfers(
             extra_pools,
-            kv_device_indices=device_indices,
+            kv_device_indices=(
+                anchor_indices if anchor_indices is not None else device_indices
+            ),
             kv_host_indices=host_indices,
         )
         if pool_transfers is None and extra_pools:
-            if need_load_kv:
+            if need_load_kv and not caller_owned:
                 full_allocator.free(device_indices)
             return None
 
@@ -1543,6 +1559,7 @@ def trim_prefetch_full_head(self, operation, trim_tokens: int) -> None:
             operation.sidecar_hash_values = original_hashes
             operation.sidecar_hit_pages = len(original_hashes)
         operation.hash_value = original_hashes[trim_pages:]
+        operation.prefetch_kv_page_offset += trim_pages
         operation.storage_hit_count -= trim_tokens
         operation.storage_start += trim_tokens

@@ -911,11 +911,29 @@ def target_reached(component_type: ComponentType) -> bool:
 
         for ct in self.tree_components:
             request_cnt = request_by_type[ct]
+            # An allocation-driven FULL request names the allocator's
+            # shortfall, not what the walk must free: an allocator can hide
+            # headroom behind a clamp (a reserve it refills before raw
+            # allocation sees a page again) or page rounding, so freeing
+            # exactly the shortfall can leave its target unmet. Such a walk
+            # runs to the target; the check after every victim still stops it
+            # at the first sufficient one.
+            to_target = (
+                ct == ComponentType.FULL
+                and request_cnt > 0
+                and available_size_targets is not None
+                and ct in available_size_targets
+            )
             # A preceding component may have cascade-evicted this component or,
             # on a shared pool, released enough bytes to satisfy its allocation.
-            if tracker[ct] >= request_cnt or target_reached(ct):
+            if target_reached(ct) or (not to_target and tracker[ct] >= request_cnt):
                 continue
-            self.tree_core.evict_device_start(ct, request_cnt)
+            walk_quota = request_cnt
+            if to_target:
+                walk_quota = max(
+                    request_cnt, tracker[ct] + self.tree_core.full_evictable_size()
+                )
+            self.tree_core.evict_device_start(ct, walk_quota)
             try:
                 while True:
                     node_id, made_progress = self._evict_device_next_node(ct, tracker)

@@ -1250,7 +1250,12 @@ def test_shorter_prefetch_reserves_full_and_swa_without_mutating_probe_keys(self
                 operation.hash_value = list(hashes)
                 operation.storage_hit_count = hit_tokens
                 operation.sidecar_hash_values = None
+                operation.prefetch_kv_page_offset = 0
                 cc.trim_prefetch_full_head(operation, hit_tokens - full_tokens)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    operation.prefetch_kv_page_offset,
+                    (hit_tokens - full_tokens) // page_size,
+                )
                 self.assertTrue(
                     cc.can_fit_prefetch_host_buffers(operation, full_tokens)
                 )

@@ -281,6 +281,63 @@ def test_state_allocation_cannot_move_a_reservation_before_its_load_is_queued(
         self.assertIn(("move", "swa"), moves)
 
 
+class TestCallerOwnedLoadDestination(_ConfigCase):
+    """A load into rows the caller already owns allocates nothing, keeps those
+    rows when it rolls back, and binds KV-derived side pools to the caller's
+    anchor rows rather than to the destination."""
+
+    def test_load_into_caller_owned_rows_allocates_nothing_and_keeps_them(self):
+        allocator, _ = _unified_swa()
+        full = allocator.full_attn_allocator
+        owned = allocator.alloc(PAGE)
+        anchor = allocator.alloc(PAGE)
+        allocated = full.allocated_count()
+        host_indices = torch.arange(PAGE)
+
+        controller = object.__new__(HybridCacheController)
+        controller.mem_pool_device_allocator = allocator
+        controller.device = "cpu"
+        controller.load_queue, controller.ack_load_queue = [], []
+        controller.mem_pool_host = SimpleNamespace(
+            entry_map={
+                PoolName.SWA: SimpleNamespace(
+                    device_alloc_fn=lambda size: None,
+                    device_free_fn=lambda indices: None,
+                    device_evict_fn=None,
+                )
+            }
+        )
+
+        # A side pool that cannot allocate cancels the load; the destination
+        # rows were never the load's to free.
+        self.assertIsNone(
+            controller.load(
+                host_indices=host_indices,
+                extra_pools=[
+                    PoolTransfer(name=PoolName.SWA, host_indices=torch.arange(PAGE))
+                ],
+                device_indices=owned,
+                anchor_indices=anchor,
+            )
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(controller.load_queue, [])
+        self.assertEqual(full.allocated_count(), allocated)
+
+        derived = PoolTransfer(name=PoolName.SWA, indices_from_pool=PoolName.KV)
+        self.assertIs(
+            controller.load(
+                host_indices=host_indices,
+                extra_pools=[derived],
+                device_indices=owned,
+                anchor_indices=anchor,
+            ),
+            owned,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(full.allocated_count(), allocated)
+        self.assertIs(controller.load_queue[-1].device_indices, owned)
+        self.assertIs(derived.device_indices, anchor)
+
+
 class TestAllocationAndTransferOrder(_ConfigCase):
     """Allocation reuses free pages without waiting on HiCache copies."""

@@ -31,6 +31,7 @@ def _build_cache(*, collateral_capacity_gain: int):
         cache.cache_controller = None
         cache.metrics_collector = None
         cache.tree_core = MagicMock()
+        cache.tree_core.full_evictable_size.return_value = 80
 
         capacity = {"available": 30}
         allocator = MagicMock()
@@ -112,6 +113,32 @@ def test_allocation_eviction_stops_when_shared_capacity_is_sufficient(self):
         self.assertEqual(result.num_tokens_evicted, 20)
         self.assertEqual(result.mamba_num_evicted, 1)
 
+    def test_allocation_eviction_runs_to_the_target_when_frees_stay_hidden(self):
+        """An allocator can hide freed pages behind a clamp or page rounding, so
+        freeing exactly the shortfall may leave its availability target unmet;
+        an allocation-driven FULL walk must keep going until the target shows."""
+        cache, capacity, leaf_count = self._build_cache(collateral_capacity_gain=0)
+        cache.tree_core.full_evictable_size.return_value = 60
+        quota = {}
+        cache.tree_core.evict_device_start.side_effect = quota.__setitem__
+
+        def next_node(component_type, tracker):
+            # The tree yields victims only up to the quota the walk opened with.
+            if tracker[component_type] >= quota[component_type]:
+                return None, False
+            return leaf_count["value"] + 1, True
+
+        cache._evict_device_next_node.side_effect = next_node
+
+        result = cache.evict_for_alloc(EvictParams(num_tokens=20))
+
+        self.assertEqual(leaf_count["value"], 2)
+        self.assertEqual(capacity["available"], 50)
+        self.assertEqual(result.num_tokens_evicted, 40)
+        cache.tree_core.evict_device_start.assert_called_once_with(
+            ComponentType.FULL, 60
+        )
+
     def test_explicit_evict_preserves_component_count_semantics(self):
         cache, _, leaf_count = self._build_cache(collateral_capacity_gain=70)
